meta.title: KoruBeni Competitive & Compliance Research
meta.scope: Personal-safety apps (global + Turkey): product, UA, monetization, revenue, Play/Apple/KVKK compliance, abuse mitigation
constraints: Every significant claim >=2 independent sources or flagged low-confidence

subject.name: KoruBeni
subject.architecture: offline-first, no developer backend, no analytics/ads, no crash SDK, RevenueCat+Play Billing for Pro

key_findings: Life360 anchors the category: USD 489.5M FY2025 revenue, USD 369.3M subscriptions, 2.8M paying circles, ~95.8M MAU, 100M+ installs [E01-E07].
Consumer pricing ladder: low-end women-safety apps USD 2-8/mo (bSafe ~USD 2-4); monitored/agent apps USD 10-20/mo (Noonlight USD 5-10, Citizen USD 19.99) [E09,E12,E14].
Turkey's dominant app is FREE government KADES (~9.7M downloads, direct police dispatch) - KoruBeni must differentiate and disclaim it is not KADES/official [E17].
Every competitor with location sharing also AUTO-SENDS location to contacts/responders; KoruBeni does not (offline-first) - largest feature gap [E10,E16,E18,E30].
Industry-standard legal posture: 'not an emergency service' + no liability for false alarms/location errors (Life360 model) [E08].

Play compliance: specialUse FGS needs declaration + demo video [E19]; Apr-2026 update pushes broad contacts to the Contact Picker and drops geofencing as special-use [E20]; stalkerware policy demands consent + persistent notification for any tracking [E22].
KVKK: Mar-2026 principle decision requires separate disclosure vs consent approvals [E23]; explicit consent must be specific/informed/free/revocable [E24].
TR consumer law: 14-day withdrawal under 6502 + Distance Contracts Regulation, limited once digital service starts; pre-purchase disclosure duties remain [E25].

hypothesis_tree.root: Can KoruBeni win a defensible niche in personal safety on Google Play / Turkey?

branches.q: Is the market monetizable for a small player?

Whether Google treats personal-safety contact lookup as a permitted broad-contacts use case or mandates the Contact Picker.
